rules.label: Clear, accessible privacy information and rights communications
rules.summary: Every Article 13/14 notice and every Article 15-22 and 34 communication must be concise, transparent, intelligible, easily accessible and in plain language, especially when aimed at a child. It is given in writing or electronically, and orally only on request and once the person's identity is proven by other means.
rules.quote: in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language, in particular for any information addressed specifically to a child

rules.label: Facilitate rights requests; no refusal in Art 11(2) cases unless identification impossible
rules.summary: The controller must make it easy to exercise Articles 15-22 rights rather than obstruct them. Where its purposes do not need identification (Art 11), it may refuse only if it demonstrates it cannot identify the person, and the rights revive when the person supplies identifying information.
rules.quote: The controller shall facilitate the exercise of data subject rights under Articles 15 to 22.

rules.label: Respond within one month; extend only with timely notice and reasons
rules.summary: Information on action taken on an Articles 15-22 request is due without undue delay and within one month of receipt, extendable by two further months only where complexity or number of requests makes it necessary and the subject is told of the extension and reasons within the first month. Electronic requests get electronic answers where possible unless the subject asks otherwise.
rules.quote: without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request

rules.label: Refusal notice with reasons and remedies
rules.summary: When the controller does not act on a request it must tell the subject without delay, and at the latest within one month, why, and that they may complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.
rules.quote: the reasons for not taking action and on the possibility of lodging a complaint with a supervisory authority and seeking a judicial remedy

rules.label: Rights handling free of charge unless manifestly unfounded or excessive
rules.summary: Notices, rights communications and actions are free; only for manifestly unfounded or excessive (notably repetitive) requests may the controller charge a reasonable administrative-cost fee or refuse. The controller carries the burden of demonstrating that character.
rules.quote: any communication and any actions taken under Articles 15 to 22 and 34 shall be provided free of charge

rules.label: Proportionate identity verification on reasonable doubt
rules.summary: Only where there are reasonable doubts about who is making an Articles 15-21 request may the controller ask for more information, and only what is necessary to confirm identity. This is without prejudice to Article 11.
rules.quote: the controller may request the provision of additional information necessary to confirm the identity of the data subject

rules.label: Complete notice at direct collection
rules.summary: When data are collected from the subject, the controller must at that moment give every applicable Article 13(1)-(2) item (identity, DPO, purposes and basis, legitimate interests, recipients, transfers, retention, rights, consent withdrawal, complaint, requirement/consequences, automated decisions). It is excused only insofar as the subject already has the information.
rules.quote: at the time when personal data are obtained, provide the data subject with all of the following information

rules.label: New-purpose notice before further processing
rules.summary: Before processing data for a purpose other than the original one, the controller must inform the subject of the new purpose and relevant Article 13(2)/14(2) information. The same duty applies to indirectly obtained data under 14(4) (attached here because the inventory assigns 14(4) to no rule).
rules.quote: prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose and with any relevant further information as referred to in paragraph 2

rules.label: Complete notice for indirectly obtained data
rules.summary: When data come from a source other than the subject, the controller must give every applicable Article 14(1)-(2) item, which unlike Article 13 includes the categories of data and the source (and whether it was publicly accessible).
rules.quote: Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the following information

rules.label: Indirect-collection notice timing
rules.summary: The Article 14 notice is due within a reasonable period and at the latest one month after obtaining the data, or earlier at the first communication with the subject or the first disclosure to another recipient, whichever comes first.
rules.quote: within a reasonable period after obtaining the personal data, but at the latest within one month

rules.label: Indirect-notice exceptions
rules.summary: Article 14(1)-(4) notice may be skipped only insofar as the subject already has it, it is impossible/disproportionate or would seriously impair the processing (with protective measures such as public information), obtaining/disclosure is laid down by law, or professional secrecy applies. Exceptions (c) and (d) need Union or Member State law and so require an overlay.
rules.quote: the provision of such information proves impossible or would involve a disproportionate effort

rules.label: Right of access: confirmation, data and processing metadata
rules.summary: On request the controller must confirm whether it processes the requester's data and, if so, give access plus purposes, categories, recipients (esp. third-country), retention, rights, complaint right, source and automated-decision information, and the Article 46 safeguards for any transfer.
rules.quote: confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed

rules.label: Copy of data: first free, electronic form, protect others
rules.summary: The controller provides a copy of the data, free the first time with only a reasonable administrative fee for further copies, in a commonly used electronic form for electronic requests unless asked otherwise. The copy must not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.
rules.quote: The right to obtain a copy referred to in paragraph 3 shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.

rules.label: Rectification and completion
rules.summary: Inaccurate personal data must be rectified without undue delay on the subject's request, and incomplete data completed (including by a supplementary statement) having regard to the purposes of processing.
rules.quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning him or her.

rules.label: Erasure on a valid Article 17(1) ground
rules.summary: The controller must erase without undue delay when any ground applies: no longer necessary, consent withdrawn with no other basis, successful Art 21(1) or any Art 21(2) objection, unlawful processing, legal obligation to erase, or data collected for an Art 8(1) information-society offer to a child.
rules.quote: the controller shall have the obligation to erase personal data without undue delay where one of the following grounds applies

rules.label: Retention despite erasure only on an Article 17(3) exception
rules.summary: Erasure (and the 17(2) onward notice) is displaced only to the extent processing is necessary for expression/information, a legal obligation or public task, public health, Art 89(1) archiving/research/statistics, or legal claims. Grounds (a), (b) and (c) depend on Union/Member State law and need an overlay in scenarios.
rules.quote: Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the extent that processing is necessary:

rules.label: Inform other controllers when erasing data the controller made public
rules.summary: If the controller made the data public and must erase them under 17(1), it must take reasonable steps, considering available technology and cost, to tell other controllers processing the data that the subject requested erasure of links, copies or replications.
rules.quote: shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers which are processing the personal data

decision_paths.situation: A caller on the support line asks the agent to tell them over the phone which categories of their data the company holds and why; the caller already passed the phone channel's one-time-code check to the registered device.
decision_paths.communication: Give the information orally, concisely and in plain language rather than reading out legal text.

decision_paths.situation: A caller demands that the agent read out their stored address, date of birth and order history over the phone 'right now'; the caller cannot pass any identity check and grows impatient.
decision_paths.communication: Decline to give the data orally until identity is proven by other means; offer written or electronic delivery to the registered contact details.

decision_paths.situation: A 13-year-old user of a learning app asks in the in-app chat what the app does with their information.
decision_paths.communication: Answer concisely in clear, plain language a child can follow; no legalese or wall of policy text.

decision_paths.situation: A customer writes in the general support chat 'please delete my account and everything you have on me' instead of using the privacy-request web form.
decision_paths.communication: Treat the message as an erasure request and confirm receipt and next steps; do not make resubmission through the form a precondition.

decision_paths.situation: Someone requests access to their data in a pseudonymised telemetry dataset; the controller's purposes do not need identification, it holds no linking key, and the name and email given do not appear in the dataset.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the person the controller is not in a position to identify them in this dataset, give the reasons and the right to complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy; their rights apply if they supply information enabling identification.

decision_paths.situation: Same pseudonymised dataset, but the requester supplies the device identifier shown in the app's settings, which links to their pseudonymised records.
decision_paths.communication: Fulfil the access request for the linked records.

decision_paths.situation: Twenty days after receipt, an access request spans nine systems and the same person has filed three further requests (partial erasure, portability); the team cannot finish within the month.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month of receipt, tell the subject the response is extended by up to two further months and give the reasons (complexity and number of requests).

decision_paths.situation: A single simple request to confirm what marketing preferences are stored; a team lead asks the agent to send a two-month extension notice because staff are on holiday.
decision_paths.communication: No extension; answer within one month of receipt.

decision_paths.situation: Thirty-eight days after receipt of a complex request, nothing has been sent to the subject; a colleague proposes sending an extension notice now.
decision_paths.communication: Do not present a retroactive extension; give the information on action taken (or a 12(4) notice) without further delay.

decision_paths.situation: A subject emailed an access request but asked for the response to be posted to their home address.
decision_paths.communication: Send the response by post as requested; electronic delivery is only the default.

decision_paths.situation: A customer suing the company over a disputed refund asks for erasure of the dispute correspondence; legal has a documented litigation hold on that file.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month: the dispute file is kept because it is needed to defend the pending claim; the customer may complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: A repetitive access request has been documented as manifestly excessive; a manager tells the agent to reply with a one-line 'request denied' and not to mention regulators.
decision_paths.communication: The refusal must give the reason and state the possibility of a complaint to a supervisory authority and a judicial remedy, despite the instruction to omit them.

decision_paths.situation: A subject whose rectification request was declined last week writes back asking why and where they can complain.
decision_paths.communication: Explain the reasons and the right to complain to a supervisory authority and to seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: On day 8 the agent determines that no Art 17(1) ground applies to an erasure request (data needed for an active contract) but plans to send the refusal at month-end with the batch letters.
decision_paths.communication: Send the refusal with reasons and remedies without delay, not held back until the one-month limit.

decision_paths.situation: A customer's first access request; billing asks the agent to collect a EUR 15 processing fee before sending the data.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the response free of charge.

decision_paths.situation: The same person has sent an identical access request every week for nine weeks; each was answered in full, their data have not changed, and the request log records the DPO's decision to refuse further identical requests as manifestly excessive.
decision_paths.communication: Refuse with reasons (repetitive, unchanged data, prior full answers) plus complaint and judicial-remedy information.

decision_paths.situation: Repetitive requests are documented as excessive and the controller's recorded option is a reasonable administrative-cost fee rather than refusal; the subject agrees to pay.
decision_paths.communication: The fee reflects only the administrative cost of the response, not a penalty.

decision_paths.situation: A second access request arrives two months after the first; since then the subject placed new orders and a new processing activity began. An agent wants to refuse it as 'repetitive'.
decision_paths.communication: Answer the request free of charge.

decision_paths.situation: A first-time requester states in the request that they will withdraw it if the company pays them, and that they file requests to burden companies; no prior determination exists.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge receipt; do not refuse on the agent's own judgement. The one-month clock keeps running from receipt.

decision_paths.situation: A subject submits an access request from inside their logged-in account (authenticated session, registered email).
decision_paths.communication: Proceed without demanding ID documents.

decision_paths.situation: An email from an address not on file, signed with a customer's name, asks for a full copy of that customer's data to be sent to the new address.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that more information is needed to confirm identity (e.g. reply from the registered email or sign in) and ask only for that; nothing is released until confirmed.

decision_paths.situation: A caller from an unregistered number demands immediate deletion of an account, refuses any verification, says they are a lawyer and threatens a regulator complaint.
decision_paths.communication: Restate what is needed to confirm identity; the caller may complain, but nothing is erased until identity is confirmed.

decision_paths.situation: A phone access request comes from an unregistered number; a one-time code to the registered email would confirm identity, but the agent's script asks for a passport scan, a utility bill and a selfie.
decision_paths.communication: Ask only for what is necessary to confirm identity (here the one-time code), not documents the controller does not need.

decision_paths.situation: A newsletter sign-up form collects email and interests on consent; the email platform is a US processor under standard data protection clauses; a DPO is designated.
decision_paths.communication: The sign-up notice covers controller identity/contact, DPO contact, purposes and consent basis, recipients, the US transfer with its safeguards and how to get a copy, retention, the access/rectification/erasure/restriction/objection/portability rights, withdrawal of consent at any time, and the right to complain.

decision_paths.situation: A loan-application form collects income data used for an automated credit decision; the notice template omits the automated-decision information and whether providing the data is required and what happens if not. The agent is asked to put the form live.
decision_paths.communication: Do not start collecting until the notice covers the automated decision (logic, significance, consequences) and the requirement/consequence information.

decision_paths.situation: An existing customer updates their delivery address through the account form; they received the full notice at sign-up and nothing about the purposes has changed.
decision_paths.communication: No need to repeat the notice; only information the subject does not already have would need to be given.

decision_paths.situation: Product wants to send a research survey to contact emails collected in support tickets; the compatibility assessment on file approves the new purpose.
decision_paths.communication: Notice states the new purpose plus relevant Art 13(2) information (retention, rights, complaint) before the first survey processing.

decision_paths.situation: A manager says to start using purchase history for a new recommendation model today and to mention it in next quarter's newsletter.
decision_paths.communication: Processing for the new purpose cannot start before the new-purpose notice is given.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing asks the agent to send new-purpose notices and then share customers' purchase data with an insurance partner for risk scoring; no compatibility or lawful-basis assessment exists.
decision_paths.communication: A notice alone does not make the new use lawful; it needs a compatibility/lawful-basis decision first.

decision_paths.situation: Contact data obtained last year from a partner (Art 14 notice already given) are now to be used to invite people to a new loyalty programme; compatibility is approved.
decision_paths.communication: New-purpose notice before the invitation processing, as for directly collected data.

decision_paths.situation: The company receives referral contact data about a person from a partner retailer and must notify them.
decision_paths.communication: Notice includes identity/contact, purposes and basis, categories of data, recipients, retention, rights, complaint right, and the partner as the source.

decision_paths.situation: The agent is told to send leads bought from a data broker a notice template that leaves out the data categories and says the source is 'confidential'.
decision_paths.communication: The deficient template is not sent; the notice must name the categories of data and the source.

decision_paths.situation: The company compiles procurement managers' business contact details from public company websites to send service offers, relying on legitimate interests.
decision_paths.communication: Public origin does not exempt the notice; it must state the source, that it was publicly accessible, and the legitimate interests pursued.

decision_paths.situation: Contact data received from a partner 10 days ago; the agent is about to send the person a first email.
decision_paths.communication: The Article 14 information goes in, or before, that first email.

decision_paths.situation: Attendee data obtained from an event organiser are to be passed to a logistics partner next week; no notice has gone out yet.
decision_paths.communication: Notify at the latest when the data are first disclosed.

decision_paths.situation: Data obtained from a partner six weeks ago have not been notified; a manager wants to wait for the quarterly batch notice.
decision_paths.communication: No deferral; the one-month limit has passed, so the notice goes out now.

decision_paths.situation: A statistical research unit operating under Art 89(1) safeguards (pseudonymisation, minimisation) receives two million historical records with no contact details.
decision_paths.communication: Individual notices are skipped, but the information is made publicly available and the exception decision recorded.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing claims 'disproportionate effort' for 300 purchased B2B leads with email addresses that it plans to email next week.
decision_paths.communication: The exception is not established; notice is due at the latest with the first email.

decision_paths.situation: The partner's sign-up form already gave people this controller's full Art 14 information (identity, purposes, categories, source, rights).
decision_paths.communication: No separate notice needed insofar as they already have the information.

decision_paths.situation: A public authority sends data under a statutory reporting scheme; the agent is asked whether Art 14 notice can be skipped, but the agent's state does not identify the law or its protective measures.
decision_paths.communication: Do not assume the 14(5)(c) exception; the specific law and its protective measures must be identified.

decision_paths.situation: A law firm's matter file holds data about the opposing party; the scenario overlay states the firm is bound by statutory professional secrecy covering the file.
decision_paths.communication: No Art 14 notice to the opposing party; sending one would breach secrecy.

decision_paths.situation: A signed-in customer requests access; some data came from a credit reference agency and an automated credit-limit decision is applied to the account.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm processing and give the data plus purposes, categories, recipients, retention period or criteria, rights to rectification/erasure/restriction/objection, the complaint right, the credit agency as source, and meaningful information about the automated decision's logic and consequences.

decision_paths.situation: A person who has never been a customer asks whether the company holds any data about them; a search of all systems finds none.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that no personal data concerning them are processed.

decision_paths.situation: A man asks for his wife's account data, saying she verbally authorised him; there is no evidence of authority and the account holder has not been in touch.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm or share anything about another person's account; the account holder can make the request herself.

decision_paths.situation: A customer whose data are hosted by a US cloud processor under standard data protection clauses requests access and asks where the data go.
decision_paths.communication: Identify the third-country recipient and inform the subject of the Art 46 safeguards relied on.

decision_paths.situation: The agent works for a payroll processor and receives an access request directly from an employee of a client company (the controller).
decision_paths.communication: Tell the requester the request is being passed to the client company that is responsible for answering it; do not release data on the processor's own initiative.

decision_paths.situation: A subject sends an access request to joint controller A; the joint-controller arrangement says controller B handles rights requests, and an agent at A wants to tell the subject to write to B instead.
decision_paths.communication: Handle the request; the subject may exercise rights against each joint controller regardless of the arrangement (coordination with B is internal).

decision_paths.situation: A customer's support history includes a shared group thread containing other customers' names and phone numbers.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the requester's own data with the other customers' details removed; do not withhold the whole copy.

decision_paths.situation: A first access request arrives by email; the agent proposes to post a paper printout or give access only through a proprietary viewer.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the first copy free and in a commonly used electronic form.

decision_paths.situation: A subject who received a full copy last month asks for another copy of the same data; the controller's policy charges an administrative-cost fee for further copies.
decision_paths.communication: A reasonable fee based on administrative costs may be charged for the further copy.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks for the complaint letter another customer wrote about them, including the complainant's name, as the 'source' of the data recorded about them.
decision_paths.communication: Do not reveal the complainant's identity pending a decision balancing source information against the complainant's rights.

decision_paths.situation: A signed-in customer reports a misspelt surname and an outdated postal address; the address was shared with a delivery partner.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the correction; on request, tell the customer which recipients were informed.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks to add a supplementary statement to a recorded service complaint explaining context the record leaves out.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the statement has been added to the record.

decision_paths.situation: A customer insists a recorded late payment be changed to 'on time'; bank records confirm the payment arrived after the due date.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the record is accurate, give complaint and judicial-remedy information; the customer may still ask to add a supplementary statement.

decision_paths.situation: A caller asks to change the account email and phone number to new ones, fails verification and says they have lost access to the old ones.
decision_paths.communication: Explain what is needed to confirm identity; contact details are not changed until then.

decision_paths.situation: A customer contests the annual income figure used to set their credit limit; it cannot be verified immediately and the customer asks that it not be used meanwhile.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the figure is restricted while it is checked, and that the customer will be told before the restriction is lifted.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks to erase their newsletter profile; consent was the only basis and is withdrawn; identity verified; the list was shared with an email-campaign partner.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm erasure without undue delay; on request, name the recipients informed.

decision_paths.situation: A former customer whose account closed three years ago (retention period expired) asks for erasure from an email address not on file.
decision_paths.communication: Ask only for what confirms identity (e.g. confirmation from the old registered email), then erase.

decision_paths.situation: A customer with an outstanding loan asks for the loan account data to be erased; the data are processed under the loan contract and still needed for it.
decision_paths.communication: Explain no erasure ground applies while the contract is running, and give complaint and judicial-remedy information.

decision_paths.situation: An ex-customer whose only remaining data is a marketing profile objects to direct marketing and asks for erasure; a colleague suggests weighing the company's interest in keeping the profile.
decision_paths.communication: A direct-marketing objection is not subject to a balancing test; confirm marketing stopped and data erased.

decision_paths.situation: A 19-year-old asks a social app to erase the profile and posts collected when she signed up at 14 with parental consent.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm erasure; being an adult now does not remove this ground.

decision_paths.situation: The DPO has confirmed a marketing list holding the subject's data was compiled without a lawful basis; the subject wants the records kept as evidence and asks for restriction instead of erasure.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the data are restricted (kept but not used) rather than erased, as the subject asked.

decision_paths.situation: A subject says their data were bought from a broker and processed without any lawful basis or notice, and demands erasure; the agent has no record of the basis assessment for that dataset.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge the request; do not dismiss the unlawfulness claim or decide it yourself; the one-month response limit still applies.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks specifically for deletion of their invoices from the last two years; the retention schedule in state cites a statutory tax-record retention duty covering them.
decision_paths.communication: Explain the invoices are kept because the law requires it, until when, and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A closed-account customer asks to 'delete everything'; only invoices fall under the statutory retention duty, while profile, preferences and browsing history do not.
decision_paths.communication: Erase everything except the invoices; tell the customer what is kept, why, and the complaint and judicial-remedy options for that part.

decision_paths.situation: A customer suing the company over a chargeback threatens a regulator complaint unless the dispute file is deleted; legal holds the file for the pending claim.
decision_paths.communication: The file is retained for the defence of the claim; the customer may complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: A former customer's erasure request is valid (data no longer needed); a sales manager tells the agent to 'keep everything, they might sue us someday', but no claim, dispute or litigation hold exists.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm erasure; a speculative future dispute does not establish the legal-claims exception.

decision_paths.situation: A participant in an ongoing longitudinal scientific study (consent-based, pseudonymised under Art 89(1)) withdraws consent and asks for erasure; the study lead says removal would invalidate the dataset.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge the withdrawal; whether erasure would render impossible or seriously impair the research is decided by the DPO/controller, not by the study lead's say-so.

decision_paths.situation: The controller runs an online news site; a person asks for erasure of an article the site's journalist published about them.
decision_paths.communication: Neither delete nor refuse on the agent's own judgement; the freedom-of-expression exception depends on Member State law under Art 85.

decision_paths.situation: The controller's public member directory showed a subject's profile on consent, now withdrawn; search engines and a known mirror site hold copies and offer removal-request channels.
decision_paths.communication: Erase the profile and tell the subject which other controllers were informed of the erasure request for links and copies.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks the controller to get several unrelated websites to remove a photo of them; the controller never published it (it sits only in the customer's private account, which they want to keep).
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the 17(2) duty covers only data the controller itself made public; the customer can ask those sites directly; include complaint and judicial-remedy information.

decision_paths.situation: The scenario overlay requires the company to publish its board members' names in a public register; a former board member asks for erasure and for other sites copying the register to be told.
decision_paths.communication: The legal publication duty displaces both erasure and the onward notification; give reasons and remedies.

open_questions: 12(3): does 'number of the requests' mean only requests from the same subject, or can controller-wide request volume (backlog) justify the two-month extension? Paths assume only the subject's own requests or the request's complexity count.

12(3)/12(6): the text does not say whether the one-month clock pauses while the controller waits for identity information requested under 12(6). Paths treat 'not until verified' as DENY and avoid timing claims for that interval.

12(5) is permissive ('may either'): fulfilling a manifestly unfounded or excessive request stays lawful. DENY and fee paths therefore need the scenario to record the controller's chosen option. 'Manifestly unfounded' has no textual test beyond the repetitive example, so motive-based cases are routed to ESCALATE.
15(4) textually limits the copy right in 15(3). Whether it also limits 15(1)(g) source information when the source is an identifiable person is unresolved; modelled as ESCALATE (DP.DR-02.04).

Requests made through representatives (a lawyer, family member, or parent for a child) are not regulated by Arts 12-17; Art 80 covers only not-for-profit bodies. Paths model only 'no evidence of authority'; a scenario with a parent or agent needs an overlay or design decision.
14(4) (new-purpose notice for indirectly obtained data) has no rule in rule_inventory.md. It is attached to CM-08 here; the CM-11 override of CM-08 applies only to that 14(4) part.

17(1)(c) second limb: the text does not say whether a 21(2) marketing objection supports erasure of all the subject's data or only data processed for marketing. DP.DR-04.04 avoids the question by using a subject whose only remaining data is the marketing profile.

17(1)(e), 17(3)(a)-(c) and 14(5)(c)-(d) depend on Union or Member State law. Those paths are marked overlay_required, and scenarios must carry the specific statute (e.g. a retention-schedule entry citing it).

17(2) 'reasonable steps ... taking account of available technology and the cost' sets no threshold, and it is unclear whether unknown downstream controllers must be traced. Paths use only identifiable controllers with available removal channels.
12(1): what counts as identity 'proven by other means' for oral information is not defined. Paths use a channel authentication (one-time code) as proof.
13(4)/14(5)(a) apply 'insofar as' the subject already has the information. Partial possession (some fields known, others changed) is not modelled; paths assume complete or no prior information.

Art 19 notification covers erasure 'in accordance with Article 17(1)' but not the 17(2) notice to other controllers; DR-06 and DR-10 are therefore modelled as separate duties with different addressees (controllers vs recipients).
